response.sql:
WITH college_counts AS (
    SELECT
        c.college_id,
        c.state,
        COUNT(DISTINCT pc.player_id) AS player_count
    FROM player_college AS pc
    JOIN college AS c
      ON c.college_id = pc.college_id
    GROUP BY c.college_id, c.state
), overall AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(player_count) AS avg_count,
        SUM(player_count) AS total_count
    FROM college_counts
)
SELECT
    cc.state,
    AVG(cc.player_count) AS avg_college_player_count,
    AVG(cc.player_count / o.avg_count) AS avg_relative_to_overall_college_average,
    AVG(cc.player_count / o.total_count) AS avg_college_share_of_total
FROM college_counts AS cc
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
GROUP BY cc.state
ORDER BY cc.state;

assumptions.assumption: A college is identified by college_id; each matching college record contributes once, and NULL or blank state values are grouped together as supplied.
The averages and shares use ordinary SQL division without rounding; the database engine's numeric division behavior applies.
